title: Split SecurityServices.cs along existing module boundaries (file gravity)
description:
Audit #9, candidate 8 (SecurityServices half) - Worth exploring. MaintenanceAgentServices half is owned by TSK-0043.

### Problem
SecurityServices.cs (1,258 lines) glues four unrelated concerns plus a stray decorator: authorization policies + permission handler (224-378), MemorySmithLocalAuthService (~466 lines, 419-885), AuditLogService with hash-chained persistence (888-1054), VersionHistoryService (1055-1188), and AuditedPageService - the IPageService decorator - hiding at line 1190 where nobody would look for it. Pure navigation friction: grep-for-filename lies about where modules live, which hurts both maintainers and AI navigation.

### Approach
Mechanical file moves along existing type boundaries; no interface or behavior changes:
AuthorizationPolicies.cs (policies + permission handler + MemorySmithExternalAuthSupport), LocalAuthService.cs, ExternalAuthOutcomeRecorder.cs, AuditLogService.cs, VersionHistoryService.cs, AuditedPageService.cs, CurrentUserContext.cs. Keep namespaces unchanged in this pass (namespace reorganization is a separate, larger conversation - see Audit #8 finding 1).

### Acceptance criteria
- git-blame-friendly pure moves; zero behavior change; suite green
- TagGovernanceTests.AuthProviderSurfaces source-inspection test updated for the new file paths
- AuditedPageService findable by filename
